summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tübingen, Tübinger Stift, and University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena, Würzburg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Munich, and Berlin, and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian, Central Asian, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Foy, and later taught Yinke Chen.
Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg, Breslau, Bonn, and Leipzig.

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, and at Munich. He held professorships at Munich and Freising, later serving as Vicar General of the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.

Friedrich Zarncke was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Rostock and Leipzig, learning under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig as privatdozent and later Rektor.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Leipzig, he held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu, served as director at the University of Vienna, and led a post at Utrecht University.

Friedrich von Spiegel was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Leipzig, Bonn, and Jena under Rückert, Fleischer, Brockhaus, and Lassen, and served as professor of oriental languages at Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University, and held academic posts at Amsterdam, SOAS, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of California, Berkeley.
Fritz Johaentgen studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at the University of Munich. He held professorships at Bonn, Munich, and Mainz, alongside visiting professorships at Córdoba, UCLA, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Chicago.

Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian positions at the Institut agronomique de Versailles, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and served as administrator at the Bibliothèque Mazarine.
Fu Yan was a scholar in philosophy and Sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College from ~1877 to 1879. He later held posts at Fudan University (~1905–1906) and Peking University (~1912).

Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and served at Academia Sinica from ~1986 to 2021.
Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University, was taught by Shili Xiong, and held a post at Tunghai University from ~1955 to 1969.
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University from ~1952 to 1960. He held academic posts at Fukuoka University (~1972–2004) and Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and other teachers. He held teaching posts at Nagoya Women's University, Aichi Gakuin University, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Fumi Yao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2011. She has held posts at the University of Tokyo, Taisho University, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Fumihiko Sueki is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, SOKENDAI, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
Fumihiro Okada is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He has served as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University.

Fumimaro Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder and H. Saddhatissa, later teaching as a professor at Kindai University and Aichi Gakuin University.
